findings.title: Select the code-review family when the legacy skill path appears
findings.body: Adding only `skills/claude-code-review/README.md` makes shard 2’s `test_code_review_identity.sh` fail. It asserts that the directory itself is absent. The changed file matches neither `skills/code-review/**` nor the four listed external files. A regression test should exercise this descendant path while the legacy directory is absent from the baseline.

findings.title: Keep the public sanitization and skill-count gates in the selected run
findings.body: Neither Makefile target runs `check-public-sanitization.py` or `check-skill-count.py`. CI invokes them separately, along with their regression tests. A tracked skill reference containing a private hostname, or a README stating the wrong skill count, can pass even a `FULL=1` selection. The disposition that whole lanes cover the content-gate findings is incorrect.

findings.title: Preserve focused tests that have no Makefile lane
findings.body: The existing selector runs `test_kimi_packet_mcp.py` for changes to `kimi_packet_mcp.py`. Neither code-review shard runs that test. The R1 example `test-public-data-acquisition-recipes.sh` is also absent from the selected lanes. Adding an unregistered executable example to its reference makes that test fail, but the rewrite would never execute it. Running a whole lane only covers its registered tests.

findings.title: Resolve the landing target before choosing the comparison range
findings.body: On a `dev`-to-`main` promotion, HEAD can equal `origin/dev` while `origin/main` lacks several commits. The nearest-base rule chooses `origin/dev`, discovers zero changed paths, and skips every lane for a nonempty PR. Explicit target or PR metadata should take precedence, with conservative selection when the target is ambiguous.

findings.title: Pass the selected base through the variable the gates consume
findings.body: `test_frozen_case_sanctity.sh` reads only `CCL_SKILL_BASE_REF`. With only `CCL_SKILL_DEFAULT_BASE_REF` set, it prints a skip and exits zero, so deleting a frozen evaluation case can pass the fast lane. `check-release-version.py` also ignores the proposed variable and falls back to `origin/dev`. Pass the resolved base through the candidate-base interface, overriding any conflicting inherited value.

findings.title: Keep candidate-base settings out of the Makefile-default regression
findings.body: I ran `test_ci_checkout_ref_binding.sh` with the proposed `CCL_SKILL_DEFAULT_BASE_REF=origin/main`. It exited 1 because its nested `make -n` must observe the repository default `origin/dev`. This test belongs to the always-selected fast lane, so the proposed propagation makes ordinary main-based runs fail on a valid checkout.

findings.title: Isolate repository-routing variables for discovery, lanes, and fixture writes
findings.body: Clearing the four named variables leaves `GIT_COMMON_DIR` and Git configuration overrides active. A hook invoking the selector can redirect ref reads to another repository or change which index and worktree the child commands inspect. Fixture `update-ref` calls are writes, so the same leak can modify real refs. The existing shared Git surface gate already enumerates these routing overrides.

findings.title: Preserve hard failures as a separate terminal result
findings.body: If a test assertion fails, the lane exits nonzero and may omit its clean token. The proposed “otherwise partial” rule gives that run the same result as a successful run with an optional lane skipped. The current selector propagates the failing exit code. Require that behavior explicitly and test it with a child that prints a success token before failing.

findings.title: Check Git metadata when the candidate has no changed paths
findings.body: An empty commit, or a commit followed by a revert, can introduce a prohibited commit message while leaving the base and HEAD trees identical. The nonempty-path condition prevents `test-repo-gates` from running at all. Its metadata gate therefore cannot provide the coverage claimed in the disposition at line 81.

findings.title: Preserve the sandbox check for changes to the sandbox runner
findings.body: The current selector runs `scripts/verify-sandbox/test.sh` for a runner change under `FULL=1` when Docker is available. The directory contract requires that test. Under the rewrite, a regression in sandbox isolation would reach neither the check nor an explicit incomplete result for it. The table’s claim that the selector already leaves this entirely manual is incorrect.

findings.title: Derive external inputs beyond path literals in the code-review scripts
findings.body: If `hooks/remind-review-covers-head.sh` starts sourcing a sibling helper, the commit introducing that dependency selects shard 1. A later change to the helper alone does not. The scanner still finds all four pinned paths while `test_review_diff.sh` executes the changed helper through the hook. Add a regression that introduces a new indirect dependency and changes only that dependency.

findings.title: Account for the updater test’s real repository contract
findings.body: `test_update_review_plan_intent.sh` passes the real repository root to `review_gate.py`. Its `repository_contract_section()` discovers tracked ancestor contracts, including root `AGENTS.md`, and attaches their contents to the packet. A root-contract edit therefore changes the input exercised by shard 2 without selecting it. I confirmed the read path, but did not establish that a particular prose edit changes the test’s final assertion.

findings.title: Keep code-review shard membership in the Makefile
findings.body: If `test-code-review` gains a third normal shard, the Makefile edit will select the family, but the selector will still invoke only `test-code-review-1` and `-2`. Every subsequent core change will miss the new shard as well. A Makefile aggregate for the normal shards would preserve the separate slow-lane policy without copying membership back into the selector.

findings.title: Distinguish an absent optional base from a failed Git operation
findings.body: In a single-branch clone with a valid `origin/main` and no `origin/dev`, probing the missing ref with `git merge-base` returns nonzero. Treating every such result as fatal rejects a usable checkout. Ignoring all probe errors instead hides corrupted history. Test the one-valid-ref case separately from a command that fails while examining an existing ref.

findings.title: Use fully qualified refs for automatic integration-base lookup
findings.body: A local branch can itself be named `origin/main`. Git’s short-ref resolution can then choose `refs/heads/origin/main` ahead of `refs/remotes/origin/main`. If the local branch points at HEAD, the selector can again exclude unpublished commits. The stale-branch test does not exercise this name collision.

findings.title: Define success evidence for each command that actually runs
findings.body: `test-repo-gates` has no terminal aggregate clean token. Its `ccl_skill_check_clean_ok` belongs to the first recipe, with many more commands following it. `npm test` has no selector-specific clean token either. Requiring every lane to print one can leave a fully successful run permanently partial. Associate each token with its producing command and check the exit status of the complete target.

findings.title: Mark incomplete coverage of untracked files in the machine-readable result
findings.body: A new untracked Markdown file with a broken link appears in discovery, but the link checker enumerates tracked paths. A warning alone still permits `select_affected_tests_ok` when the other selected commands succeed. Staging the identical bytes then turns the check red. Report the unchecked input as partial or validate it before issuing the clean token.

findings.title: Validate dependency changes against the candidate npm lockfile
findings.body: With `node_modules` present, a dependency edit inconsistent with `package-lock.json` can pass `npm test` against the previous install and fail CI’s `npm ci`. A note about the stale install does not change the proposed clean result. Also preserve the existing `--with-npm` bootstrap on a fresh checkout, where `npm test` alone cannot rely on a local compiler or dependencies.

findings.title: Preserve the distinct npm pack command under full verification
findings.body: The current selector runs `npm run test:pack` for an affected package with slow tests enabled, and CI invokes that command separately. `npm test` exercises pack tests but does not invoke the `test:pack` package script. Breaking that script’s command can therefore leave the rewritten full run green while the CI pack step fails.

findings.title: Exercise the negative selection path and the repository-required full run
findings.body: This branch changes `Makefile` relative to `origin/main`, so execution here selects the code-review family. The additional replay also selects it. Neither execution would catch a runner that ignores a correct dry-run decision and always launches the shards. Use a controlled skip case and a failing child, and run the root contract’s `make test`. Line 90’s `make test-repo-gates` alone omits two required lanes.

findings.title: Replay the same selection predicate used in the savings estimate
findings.body: I replayed the 115 first-parent merges on `origin/main`. The stated four-file predicate produces 61 skips, but three of those merges touched `.github/`, which line 54 selects. The proposed rules therefore skip at most 58 of 115 before accounting for additional dependencies. The estimate also uses CI timings that include job setup and abort-leak legs that the default selector skips even for affected changes.
